# Limitations {#sec-limitations}

**The result is about training, and holds at the end of it.** Window-Bayes minimises expected squared error (@prp-optimal), so a network that optimised its loss exactly would match it by construction. H1 and H2 establish that this network, on this schedule, gets there; they do not discover that networks are rational. And they hold at step {{< var design.steps >}} only, the checkpoint at which the cosine learning rate has reached zero. At {{< var design.step_mid >}} steps the windowed models are equivalent on at most {{< var trace.windowed.max_equivalent_early >}} of {{< var h2.n_total >}} verdicts per window, with excess errors of up to {{< var trace.windowed.max_mse_early >}} points (exploratory; @sec-exploratory). A different schedule, a shorter budget or a harder process could leave departures that look like bias and are under-training. The pre-registered guard, re-training any flagged finding at {{< var design.steps_long >}} steps, was aimed at differences, and none arose; it was never a test that the equivalences are stable under more or less training, and no such test was run.

**One architecture.** The confirmatory claims are about this network: a pre-normalisation causal transformer with an output head affine in the current value. Before the freeze, a probe at one seed of a small model showed that a linear head reading a layer-normalised state could not scale its forecast with $x_t$, leaving {{< var prefreeze.linear_r1_mse >}}% excess error at ρ = 1 ({{< var prefreeze.linear_r1_mse_w4 >}}% in a windowed cell); the affine head removed that ({{< var prefreeze.affine_r1_mse >}}% and {{< var prefreeze.affine_r1_mse_w4 >}}%). The choice was made on that failure at ρ = 1 and not on the sign of any gap at ρ = {{< var design.h3.rho_lo >}} or {{< var design.h3.rho_hi >}}, where every variant in the probe showed a small negative gap, but the tables on which it was made did include those rows (@sec-prereg, [Appendix @sec-app-disclosures]). The paper does not say that transformers in general, or this network with a linear head, behave this way. The affine head also builds in the functional form of the optimum, a slope on the current value, which may make the optimum easier to reach than it would be for a head without it.

**Capacity.** The smallest model ({{< var design.size.xs.layers >}} layer, width {{< var design.size.xs.d >}}) departs from its benchmarks on {{< var size.xs.total.different >}} of {{< var size.n_per_size >}} verdicts, towards a middling persistence (exploratory; @sec-exploratory). The statement that the network matches its information-matched Bayesian holds here from {{< var design.size.s.layers >}} layers and width {{< var design.size.s.d >}} upward, and only size l was registered to carry it.

**Simulated evidence.** Every confirmatory claim is about networks trained and tested on simulated AR(1) data with a known, correctly specified prior. Nothing here says how a large language model behaves, or a person. The arms that would have probed misspecification, a mismatched prior and a mid-sequence break in ρ, were dropped at the sign-off.

**The human overlay does not test people.** In the unknown-mean family that is closest to the experiment, the matched Bayesian itself overreacts at high persistence, so the premise of H3 does not carry over, and the human intervals include the four-observation Bayes curve from ρ = {{< var overlay.first_rho_incl_w4 >}} upward. The overlay therefore does not show people overreacting beyond an information-limited Bayesian; nor does it show that they are one. It compares curves computed on different data, with a window fixed by a budget decision and priors not matched to the experiment (@sec-overlay). The survey comparison of @sec-spf is weaker still and is not a test of anything.

**What the interval does not contain.** The seed is the unit, and every seed is scored on the same evaluation sets. The intervals measure variation across training runs; the sampling error of the evaluation sets is common to all seeds and is not in them. Model and benchmark are compared on the same pairs and the sets are large, but that error is not quantified in this paper; a bootstrap over evaluation sequences would do so. With {{< var design.n_seeds >}} seeds the intervals also rest on a t distribution with four degrees of freedom and on the seeds being exchangeable draws, which a handful of runs cannot check. Cells at the same seed share their training paths, so agreement across windows is not independent corroboration.

**Self-registration and the timing of deviations.** The pre-registration is a tagged document in the author's repository. It was not lodged with an independent registry, and the repository and its tags were made public on {{< var meta.public_date >}}, after every run had finished, so the tag dates are the author's record and not an independent timestamp. The freeze ({{< var prereg.tag.v1.name >}}) and the budget deviation ({{< var prereg.tag.v11.name >}}) preceded any confirmatory run. The incomplete-seed rule ({{< var prereg.tag.v12.name >}}) and the survey-comparison rules ({{< var prereg.tag.v13.name >}}, {{< var prereg.tag.v14.name >}}) were fixed after confirmatory runs had started and their metrics files and per-run logs existed, but before the analysis code had been run on any real metrics and before any trained model saw survey data (@sec-prereg, [Appendix @sec-app-deviations]). Neither bears on a confirmatory number as things turned out: no seed group was incomplete, and the survey comparison is illustrative.

**Budget cuts.** The grid as run is smaller than the grid as frozen ({{< var runs.planned >}} of {{< var design.runs.configured >}} runs). Size m and Family B have {{< var runs.m_seeds >}} seeds per cell; neither enters a decision. The three earliest checkpoints were dropped, which thins the exploratory training traces. Moving the two small sizes to a laptop and cutting size m were the pre-registered responses to an over-budget pilot; the other cuts were not foreseen, though all were decided from timing alone and before any confirmatory run. The {{< var runs.primary >}} primary runs were not cut.

**Resumed runs, lost checkpoints and arithmetic.** {{< var runs.n_resumed >}} of the {{< var runs.planned >}} runs were resumed from a saved checkpoint after an interruption. A resume restores the model, optimiser and scheduler state and batches are seeded by step, so a resumed run follows the same data stream; no run failed in the end. The checkpoints of {{< var runs.n_lost_ckpt >}} size-l runs (all five at W = 8 and one at W = 4) were lost with a cloud instance after their evaluation files had been copied, so those verdicts can be recomputed from the files but the models cannot be re-evaluated. The cloud cells were trained and evaluated with TF32 matrix multiplication: re-evaluating two of them in full precision moved excess error by up to {{< var tf32.max_mse_shift >}} points and the gap by up to {{< var tf32.max_gap_shift >}}, far inside the margins but of the order of the fourth decimal reported here.

**The literature search.** The claim that the combination studied here is new rests on a search with stated blind spots (@sec-literature).
